_note: THE TWO-STEP PERMISSION LADDER, enforced rather than documented (parity/F09-geo.md §3a). Asking for `always` cold is denied by most users, and it is flagged in App Store and Play review; both platforms are built on the assumption that an app earns background location AFTER it has demonstrated the foreground case. So the module makes the correct sequence the ONLY sequence: a cold `always` refuses with escalation_required and never reaches a prompt. This corpus pins the state machine every renderer shares (TS GeoPolicy.permissionPlan/applyPermission, Kotlin :core GeoPolicy, Swift Engine/iOS GeoPolicy), including the case libraries get wrong in the other direction: a user who DECLINES the escalation. iOS shows the Always prompt exactly once, so a second request cannot prompt; the honest answer is to settle with the whenInUse the app still holds and prompted:false, not to spin a dialog that will never appear.

plan.name: whenInUse when already granted settles without prompting again
whenInUse while holding always settles at always
whenInUse after a denial refuses, because the OS will not prompt twice
whenInUse under parental or MDM restriction refuses
A COLD ALWAYS IS REFUSED - the ladder is enforced, not suggested
always after a denied whenInUse is still escalation_required, never a second prompt
always ON TOP of a granted whenInUse is the one legal escalation
always after the user declined the escalation settles at whenInUse, prompted:false
plan._note: The case every library gets wrong. iOS offers the Always prompt ONCE; asking again shows nothing. Resolving with the truth - you still hold whenInUse, and no dialog appeared - lets an app route the user to Settings instead of waiting for a callback that will never come.

plan.name: always under restriction refuses as denied, not as an escalation problem
an unrecognised level is refused, never defaulted to the safer one
the level vocabulary is exact case

apply.name: granting the whenInUse prompt lands at whenInUse
declining the whenInUse prompt lands at denied, and the ladder is over
granting the escalation lands at always and records that it was offered
DECLINING THE ESCALATION KEEPS whenInUse and burns the one offer
apply._note: This is what a denied `always` after a granted `whenInUse` MEANS: the app did not lose foreground location, and it will never be offered the upgrade again in-app. The next honest move is a Settings deep link, which is why the state records escalationOffered rather than throwing the grant away.

apply.name: a second escalation attempt cannot un-burn the offer

_note_route: THE ANDROID BACKGROUND SPLIT. `always` is ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION, a separate runtime permission since Android 10 - and from Android 11 (API 30) the system REFUSES to show it in a normal request dialog at all: the only path is the app settings screen. An app that calls requestPermissions and waits for a callback waits forever. The route is therefore part of the contract, not an implementation detail.

route.name: Android 11 must send the user to Settings
Android 14 must send the user to Settings
the web has no background location at all

_note_precise: iOS 14 and Android 12 both let a user grant APPROXIMATE location while accepting the permission. An app that needs precision (turn-by-turn, a fitness track) must know, so `precise` is requested explicitly and a reduced grant is the typed precise_denied rather than a stream of 3-kilometre fixes that look like a bug in the app.

precise.name: precision not requested, and not granted, is fine
precision not requested but granted anyway is fine
precision requested and reduced is a typed refusal
